text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - UK shares were firm at the close, underpinned by fresh gains in the Dow and U.S. Treasury bonds but well below the day's early record amid caution ahead of Thursday's election. After touching a record 4,466.5 in early trade, the FTSE 100 coasted lower for much of the day to close up just 2.8 points at 4,436.0 -- short of the record close of 4,444.3 set on March 11.

FRANKFURT - German shares bounded higher in bourse trade in a delayed response to post-bourse gains from Tuesday when benign U.S. data were seen as reducing the imminent need for a U.S. interest rate rise. German gains nonetheless failed to match the sharp 2.6 percent rise in the Dow Jones as scepticism over U.S. stock gains continued. The DAX-30 index of leading German shares ended the session up 54.88 points, or 1.6 percent, at 3,438.07, some 14 points off its session high of 3,452.61. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,438.09. up 12.23.

PARIS - French shares closed sharply higher on Wednesday in big volume boosted by options expiry after it shrugged off a decline in the afternoon on stronger than expected U.S. economic growth. The Bourse, which is closed on Thursday for the May Day holiday, started with a 1.47 percent gain, building on Tuesday's two percent advance due to a jump on Wall Street as data on labour costs and durable goods dispelled inflation fears. The CAC-40 index closed up 1.41 percent at 2639.46, a rise of 36.60 points.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended at a record high after overcoming a brief period of temporary weakness that followed the afternoon release of U.S. GDP data. The indices broke new ground, continuing the recent record run. The fact that the Dow Jones held up well in early trade helped the shares. "But there is still some insecurity around, due mainly to the fact that Wall Street, unlike Zurich, will be open on May 1," one dealer said. The Swiss bourse will be closed on Thursday for the Labour Day holiday. The Swiss Market Index (SMI) was up 42.5 points, or 0.88 percent, to 4,897.6. A new intraday high was reached at 4,903.5. The Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 23.70 points, or 0.77 percent, to 3,094.65.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks surged upwards, with the key index ending up nearly 500 points at its highest close in four months. The rally was inspired by a surge on Wall Street on Tuesday and the yen's weak trend against the dollar. Plans by a number of firms to buy back their own shares, announced in recent weeks, also brightened the market. The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended up 480.75 points or 2.57 percent at 19,151.12. A few minutes before the close it had opened up a 500-point gap from Monday's close.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks posted their biggest point gain in more than two months on Wednesday after U.S. economic data calmed fears about higher interest rates and triggered an overnight surge on Wall Street. The blue chip Hang Seng index jumped 302.88 points, or 2.40 percent, to close at 12,903.30, just slightly off the day's high of 12,924.27.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market reached new peaks on Wednesday before an avalanche of afternoon profit-taking wiped out most of the early gains by the close. The All Ordinaries index added 8.9 points to 2,488.0 after touching a record high of 2,515.1 shortly after the market opened. This surpassed the previous record high of 2,508.3 reached on February 19, 1997.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares staged a late rally on Thursday as futures related buying helped shed their earlier losses to finish firmer. Gold shares sank to fresh four-year lows as woes on the weak bullion price pervaded the market. Dealers said the local market was generally quiet in the afternoon session ahead of the Workers Day market holiday on Thursday. The overall index ended up 23.5 points at 7,130.5, the industrial index gained 41.5 points to 8,494.3 points and the gold index dropped 18.2 points to fresh four-year low of 1,187.0 points.
